summary: The lecture defines GDP and explains three calculation methods: value added, income, and expenditure. It distinguishes GDP from GNP using net factor income from abroad, derives NDP and NNP by subtracting depreciation, and converts market price to factor cost via indirect taxes and subsidies. It also covers personal vs national income, real vs nominal GDP, GDP deflator, and key difficulties in national income measurement.
points: GDP = total final value of goods/services produced within domestic territory in a specific period.
Three GDP calculation methods: Value Added, Income, Expenditure.
Expenditure method: GDP = C (household) + I (private) + G (government) + (X - M).
GDP estimated by Central Statistical Office under Ministry of Statistics & Programme Implementation.
GNP = GDP + Net Factor Income from Abroad (factor income from abroad minus to abroad).
NDP = GDP – Depreciation; NNP = GNP – Depreciation.
NNP at Factor Cost = NNP at Market Price – Indirect Taxes + Subsidies.
Personal Income includes transfer payments (pensions, subsidies) excluded from National Income.
Real GDP uses base-year prices; Nominal GDP uses current prices; GDP deflator indexes price changes.
Major measurement difficulties: double counting, self-consumption, illegal activities, depreciation estimation, unpaid household services.
